_readme: VERIFICATION REGISTRY. A behaviour change whose proof needs a story run gets an entry here in the same push (pre-push gate scripts/admin/check-verify-coupling.js; escape: a `Verify: none (<reason>)` or `Verify: <entry-id>` commit trailer). After ANY validation run: `node scripts/admin/verify-run.js <storyId> [--env=prod] --write` judges every pending entry against that stored run and prints CONFIRMED / FAILED / HUMAN / NOT COVERED. A run is evidence only for commits its recorded build (stories.data.analytics.build.commitFull) contains; an absent run shape (no over-the-shoulder page, no iterate repair ...) is NOT COVERED, never a pass. Fields: id; title; commits (every one must be in the run's build); addedAt; claim (what a new run must show, one sentence); runShape (all must hold: any | full-story | trial | age-band:N (or N|M) | needs-shot:<shot> | needs-iterate-repair | needs-char-fix | needs-inpaint | needs-fresh-idea | needs-worn-off | needs-fresh-avatar-sheet | needs-composite — defined in scripts/admin/verify-checks.js SHAPES); check ({kind:'auto', fn} names a function in verify-checks.js, {kind:'human', what} says what to look at); status (pending | confirmed | failed | superseded); evidence[] (appended by verify-run.js --write or --mark; never edited by hand, never deleted). An auto FAILED stays pending and is printed loudly; only a human --mark sets failed. Entries are never deleted: a change that is replaced becomes superseded with a note.

entries.claim: On the next staging story: every REQUIRED OBJECTS line for a VB creature/object/vehicle in a knee-high..house-height band carries a yardstick against the named figures in frame (body landmark or multiple), every melon-sized-or-smaller one names a body part of the figure touching it (else the first figure in frame), and the precedence line follows; the stored quality eval input ELEMENT SIZES carries the same sentences; the elements render near that size (no creature at half or less / twice or more, no held prop at 2x or more).

check.what: sceneImages[].imageVersions[].prompt REQUIRED OBJECTS lines vs VB scaleClass; look at every page with a cited element and compare its size to the named figure/body part. Baselines: run 7 job_1790277448294_5herh01j7 p9/p11 (egg melon-sized, dragon waist-high), run 8 job_1790373080139_vnx5l8iy7 p10 (grown dragon). A/B bodies: image stage, params.variants current-build (pageScaleScope {types:[animal],bands:[adult-height,twice-adult-height]}) vs new-build.

entries.title: The Art Director gives a melon-sized-or-smaller prop a hand or body contact wherever the story allows it
entries.claim: On the next staging story with a small VB prop: on pages where the story has a figure hold, carry or keep it, the brief carries an interactions row naming the prop (held, carried, in a lap, against a chest); pages where the story places it away from people carry no such row; the prop renders at its size on the contact pages.

check.what: sceneDescriptions[].description METADATA interactions[] rows naming the small prop id, against the page text; view each page image. Baseline: EXACT POSES rider on job_1789584708605_rts4wqupm - right size 6/6 with contact, oversized 3/3 without.

entries.title: Every per-page plate is judged on a text-below story, with a null text position
entries.claim: On the next staging story (text-below layout): every page plate rendered by renderPagePlate (a page not covered by a vantage) has a plate_qc eval_calls row labelled P<n> (retry P<n>-retry when it failed), no text_area finding, and a failing plate carries emptySceneQc (v1Issues, keptAttempt) on its page record; a plate with people or a photographic medium is flagged figures / medium.

check.what: eval_calls kind plate_qc for the story: one row per per-page plate label P<n>; story_images empty_scene plates viewed against their verdicts; stored sceneImages[].emptySceneQc on failed ones. Baseline: staging job_1790277448294_5herh01j7 had no per-page plate QC at all.

entries.title: Every real-landmark plate cites its landmark photo, and the page is served exactly that slot
entries.claim: On the next staging story with a real landmark: every real-landmark vantage (or vantage-less landmark location) in stories.data.visualBible carries landmarkPhoto (a servable photo number or "none"), the genLog has no landmark_photo_citation warning, and each page's stored landmarkPhotos[].variantNumber equals the landmarkPhoto of the vantage whose pages name it (no photo where it cites "none").

check.what: visualBible.locations[].vantages[].landmarkPhoto vs sceneImages[].landmarkPhotos[].variantNumber per page; generationLog for landmark_photo_citation; view the cited photo against the vantage emptyScenePrompt (does it show what the plate frames?). Baseline: staging job_1790277448294_5herh01j7 — p1 (stairs up to the square) was served the chess-square photo, no citation existed.

entries.title: A failed pipeline char-fix records which gate refused it
entries.claim: On the next staging story with a failed char-fix round: its sceneImages[].retryHistory round_repair_failed entry and repairRounds pages[].error name the gate (blend_gate / style_drift / repaired_figure_blurred / repair_unnatural / face_integrity) and its message — no entry reads exactly "char-fix produced no usable image".

check.what: stories.data sceneImages[].retryHistory (type round_repair_failed, method char-fix) and repairRounds[].pages[].error; the Railway log line "🚫 [CHAR-FIX] Page N <name>: …". Baseline: staging job_1790446348343_z3fw660ie carried the bare sentence.
